title: Getting Louis a trumpet; Buster Bailey joins
summary: Scott and Chambers take Armstrong downtown for a trumpet; Buster Bailey arrives, completing the band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So we gradually got Louis -- oh, I'm a little ahead of my story. He had a cornet. Now, cornet is for a band, that was playing shrill. A trumpet is more mellow. Elmer and I took him downtown one day, we met him because Fletcher was beginning to play about Louis blowing so loud. He only had a cornet. We took him downtown, and we got him a trumpet. Well, he didn't know where to go, and we went down and got him a trumpet.

Well, he adjusted to that right away, because he had music in him. It was just a different horn, that was all. And so that made the band a little more even, three trumpets. So we continued and continued. In the meantime, there were rumors going around about Duke. Well, I didn't know what they meant and everything. And Fletcher -- oh, Louis came first. I was so busy talking about Louis I forgot about Buster.
Buster got there in time to open up in Roseland, so we had a full band then. Before that, it had just been Don Readman and Coleman Hawkins. Now, that made a trio then, and he
was excellent on that clarinet. Well, musicians came from far and wide just to see his band. But Duke was coming up, slowly but surely.
